processing: Black tea made from highland leaf; the estate also turns out white, green, flavoured and herbal lines. Details of the methods are little documented.
harvest_season: Little is documented on prized pickings; no single season defines the tea.
appearance_dry: Dark, fine leaf, as is usual for a highland estate black tea sold mainly in bags and small packs.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a highland black tea.
appearance_wet: Small coppery-brown leaf, as expected of this type.
taste_profile: Few independent tasting notes exist; expect the light-to-medium, clean highland black tea usual for the Cameron Highlands, with mild astringency.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for a bagged or small-leaf black tea. Drink it plain first, then try it with milk.

vintage_note: Sold under the Cameron Valley brand as a year-round packaged tea, in bags and small boxes, with no vintage or season stated. As with most packaged black teas, go by the best-before date and buy fresh.
description:
Bharat is a tea plantation in Malaysia's Cameron Highlands, and its tea reaches shoppers as Cameron Valley. It is often called the second-largest estate in the highlands, and it sits within about ten kilometres of its better-known neighbour, BOH.

The range is broader than the black tea it is listed under here: white, green, flavoured and herbal teas are sold too, along with a premium line called Premium Gold.

Few tasting notes get beyond tourist impressions, so assume the usual highland profile, clean and fairly light. Keep the steep short if you brew it plain.

This is everyday packaged tea at everyday prices, not a connoisseur's estate. The most rewarding way to meet it is at the roadside tea house, with the slopes in view.
history:
The plantation is dated to 1933, with the Bharat Group as its owner. The founder is credited to an Indian-born entrepreneur, though the accounts differ on the name and the family, so that part is uncertain.

The Cameron Valley brand came decades later, 61 years after the plantation began by one business report, which also gives the estate 1,600 acres. The group has since spread into oil palm, property and logistics.
